note: Every hard leap, up and down, from a new Do each time, found from its neighbour (Sol or the next Do); the second section takes the picture of the voice away, the one thing it changes. Folded in from the two unseen-leaps drills.

exercise.title: Every hard leap, up and down
exercise.why: With Do in a new key each time you can't lean on the last note you sang, so each leap has to be found from its neighbour: Sol, or the next Do.

cells.text:
Press Start below to hear Do and start the mic. Any hard leap can come: the minor 3rd, the tritone, the minor 6th or a 7th, up or down, and Do moves to a new key each time.
Name the neighbour before you sing: Sol for the tritone and the minor 6th, the next Do for the 7ths. Then sing the landing note on "oo" and hold it until Yes shows, and press Next below for another leap.
If a leap down misses, press Restart below and hear the landing note in your head first.

Press Start below. The same leaps come, and your voice is not drawn: the game shows only whether your note counted. Hear the neighbour and then the landing note in your head, then sing it on "oo" and hold it until Yes shows.
Practice until the leaps land without you thinking of a neighbour first.
